items.text: The US Treasury Department reported that Chinese hackers infiltrated its systems in a state-sponsored cyberattack. Officials revealed to Congress that the breach occurred in December when hackers exploited software vulnerabilities in third-party software. Ryan Kalember, a cybersecurity expert, explained that the attackers exploited flaws in software designed to manage privileged accounts remotely. This allowed them access to sensitive but unclassified documents. This attack follows a pattern of Chinese state actors targeting supply chains and cybersecurity tools. China denies involvement and opposes hacking. Although described as a major incident, Kalember noted it is less severe than other cyberattacks, as no classified information was accessed. He warned, however, that supply chain attacks pose ongoing challenges for the US government due to reliance on third-party vendors. Difficult words: infiltrate (to enter secretly), exploit (to make use unfairly to get an advantage), flaw (a mistake or problem), unclassified (not secret). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The US Treasury Department says Chinese hackers attacked its computers. Officials told Congress that in December, hackers broke in by using problems in third-party software. China denies this and says it doesn’t support hacking. Ryan Kalember, a cybersecurity expert, explained that hackers used mistakes in software to control important accounts. This gave them access to sensitive but not secret information. He said these kinds of attacks happen often, and they target big organizations. Kalember said the attack was serious but not as bad as some others. The hackers didn’t steal any secret information, but the US government must improve security to prevent future attacks. Difficult words: break in (to get into), deny (to say that something is not true), sensitive (important and private), target (to select for an attack). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US Treasury Department says Chinese hackers break into its computers. This happens in December. Hackers used a problem in third-party software. China says it is not true. An expert, Ryan Kalember, says hackers use a software problem to get into important accounts . They take the information. Luckily, this information is not secret. Kalember says that this type of attack is usual. It happens often to big groups. The expert says the attack is bad, but not the worst. The US government needs to work harder to stop hackers from using third-party software to break in again. Difficult words: break into (to get into), third-party (a person or group besides the two main persons or groups), account (detailed information about all the money of a business or a person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Actors Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt have finalized their divorce settlement, concluding an eight-year legal battle that captivated Hollywood. Jolie’s lawyer announced on Tuesday that the settlement had been signed and filed, though no details had been disclosed. Pitt’s representatives haven’t commented. The couple, married for only two years, separated in 2016 when Jolie cited irreconcilable differences. She initially sought full physical custody of their six children, leading to a custody battle. Pitt faced and was cleared of child abuse allegations during the dispute, with both sides accusing each other of media manipulation. They eventually agreed to equal custody through a private judge. Jolie, an Oscar-winning actress, was previously married to Johnny Lee Miller and Billy Bob Thornton. Pitt, also an acclaimed actor, was married to Jennifer Aniston before meeting Jolie on the set of Mr. and Mrs. Smith, sparking rumors of an affair that Jolie denied. Difficult words: captivate (to attract and hold the interest and attention), irreconcilable (unable to fix), acclaimed (publicly praised). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt ended their divorce case after eight years. Jolie’s lawyer announced the settlement on Tuesday, but he didn’t share any details of the agreement. The actors married in 2014 but separated in 2016. Jolie asked for full custody of their six children, which led to a long legal fight. Police investigated Pitt for child abuse but cleared him. Later, the actors agreed to share custody equally . Both said the other of using the media to get public support. Before their marriage, Pitt was with Jennifer Aniston, and Jolie was married twice. They met while filming Mr. and Mrs. Smith. Difficult words: settlement (agreement), custody (taking care of children), equally (fairly and in the same way). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt are now officially divorced. Jolie’s lawyer says that the actors sign the deal. We do not know any details of the deal. Jolie and Pitt are married for two years but split up in 2016. Jolie wants full custody of their six kids. This leads to a long fight. Police check Pitt for child abuse but find nothing. Later, the two agree to share custody. Before Jolie, Pitt’s wife is actress Jennifer Aniston. Jolie is married twice before. They meet while making the movie Mr. and Mrs. Smith. Some people think they have an affair , but Jolie says they are just friends. Later, they are together. Difficult words: custody (taking care of children), child abuse (behaving badly towards children), affair (romantic relationship). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Amal Alabadla, a resident of Gaza, gave birth to her son Mohamed on October 7, 2023, amid the chaos of war. Her eldest son, Noah, was only 18 months old. Since then, Amal has endured constant bombardments, food shortages, and multiple displacements while caring for her children. Her husband, who works in the West Bank, hasn’t been able to return home since before the conflict began. As a result, he has never met their newborn son. Amal described her struggles, including fleeing airstrikes and living in temporary shelters under harsh conditions. She recalled holding her sons tightly during bombings and trying to stay strong despite her inner pain. Israel claims it is dismantling terrorist networks in Gaza and doesn’t target civilians. Meanwhile, Amal says her children’s smiles give her the strength to continue fighting for a better future for them. Difficult words: endure (to suffer through), displacement (being forced to leave home), dismantle (to take apart). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Amal Alabadla lives in Gaza and had her son Mohamed on October 7, 2023. Her older son, Noah, was 18 months old at the time. Amal is going through bombing, food shortages , and moving from place to place while taking care of her children. Her husband works far away in the West Bank and can’t come home, so he never met Mohamed. Amal spoke about escaping bombing and living in shelters . She tries to be strong for her children but feels very unhappy inside. Israel says it doesn’t attack people and is fighting terrorist groups. Amal says her children’s smiles give her hope and strength to keep going. Difficult words: shortage (not enough of something), escape (to get away), shelter (a safe place to stay). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Amal Alabadla lives in Gaza. She has her baby, Mohamed, on October 7, 2023. Her older son, Noah, is just 18 months old. Amal is having a hard time because of the bombing , no food, and moving from place to place. Amal’s husband is far away in the West Bank. He cannot come home because of the war. He never meets baby Mohamed. Amal says it is very scary . She holds her children close during bombs and tries to stay strong for them. Israel says it does not hurt people and is fighting dangerous groups. Amal says her children make her happy and help her keep going. Difficult words: bombing (dropping bombs), scary (making you feel frightened). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The decades-long agreement for Russian gas to flow to the EU via Ukraine has ended as a five-year contract between Ukraine’s Naftogaz and Russia’s Gazprom expired. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky refused to extend it, stating it helped fund Russia’s war. The EU was given a year to prepare, and the European Commission says its gas system is resilient . However, Slovakia might face challenges, and Moldova is already experiencing shortages. Gas now reaches Hungary, Turkey, and Serbia through the TurkStream pipeline. Russia’s long history of supplying cheap gas to Europe, dating back to 1964, has almost entirely stopped. Most EU gas now comes from alternative sources like the US, Norway, and Qatar, although it is much costlier. European consumers pay up to four times more than in the US, which impacts the region’s economic competitiveness . Difficult words: resilient (able to recover or adjust quickly), entirely (completely), competitiveness (the ability to compete successfully). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The deal for Russian gas to go through Ukraine to the EU is over. This happened because Ukraine’s President Zelensky refused to allow more gas. He said it supported Russia’s war. The EU had a year to prepare, and the European Commission says it can handle this change. But some countries, like Slovakia, may have problems, and Moldova already has less gas. Gas now comes to Hungary, Turkey, and Serbia using the TurkStream pipeline. For many years, Russia supplied cheap gas to Europe, but now the EU gets gas from other countries like the US and Norway. This gas is more expensive, and EU citizens pay much more than Americans. Difficult words: refuse (to say no), supply (to give or provide), citizen (a person of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The deal for Russian gas through Ukraine ends. Ukraine’s president, Zelensky, says no to more gas from Russia. He says that it helps Russia in the war. The EU is ready for this. It says that things will be okay. But some countries have problems, for example, Slovakia and Moldova. Moldova does not have enough gas right now. Now, gas comes to some countries through another pipeline called TurkStream. Before, Europe has cheap gas from Russia. Now, the EU buys gas from places like the US and Norway. But this gas costs more money. People in Europe pay higher prices than people in America. Difficult words: deal (when countries or organizations do business together), pipeline (a tube for sending gas or liquid). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Poland has taken over the rotating presidency of the EU Council following Hungary’s term. Prime Minister Donald Tusk aims to focus on consensus -building, emphasizing security and defense during Poland’s six-month leadership. The agenda includes ensuring energy, economic, and food security while addressing disinformation. Foreign policy experts consider Poland’s leadership timely due to Europe’s current security challenges. Poland’s priorities include stronger support for Ukraine, boosting European arms production, and integrating military industries. As a border state with Kaliningrad, Belarus, and Ukraine, Poland has increased its defense spending and influence in NATO and the EU since the Ukraine war began. The rivalry between Tusk and President Andrzej Duda could impact Poland’s EU agenda , especially with upcoming elections. Difficult words: consensus (agreement among a group), timely (happening at the best possible moment), rivalry (competition), agenda (a list of matters to be discussed at a formal meeting). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Poland is leading the EU Council for the next six months. This comes after Hungary’s time and many arguments with EU countries. Prime Minister Donald Tusk plans to focus on security and peace. Poland wants to improve energy, food, and economic safety and fight against fake news. Poland will also work to help Ukraine, make more weapons in Europe, and connect military industries. Poland is a neighbor to Russia and Ukraine and spends a lot on defense . Since the Ukraine war started, the country became an even more important NATO and EU member. Inside Poland, politics could make things harder. Prime Minister Tusk and President Duda have different views, and elections are coming soon. Poland hopes to do well as EU leader. Difficult words: argument (when people don’t agree or fight), military (about soldiers and the army), defense (actions to protect a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Poland is leading the EU for the next six months. Prime Minister Donald Tusk says Poland will help make Europe safe. The country wants to protect energy, food, and money. It will also help stop fake news. Poland is a neighbor of Russia and Ukraine. It spends a lot of money to protect itself. Since the start of the war in Ukraine, Poland is more important in Europe and NATO. Inside Poland, there are two leaders with different ideas. Prime Minister Tusk and President Duda do not always agree. This could make Poland’s job in the EU harder. Difficult words: protect (to keep safe), fake (not real), neighbor (a country or place next to another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A massive steer towers among its regular counterparts , being almost 2 meters tall and weighing a whopping 1.4 tonnes. Thanks to its size, the enormous animal named Knickers escaped the slaughterhouse because it is simply too big. It will live out its days in the paddocks of Lake Preston in Perth, Australia. Difficult words: steer (a bullock – a castrated bull), counterpart (someone similar to you), whopping (very large), enormous (very large in size), paddock (a small field for animals). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A massive bullock in Australia escaped the slaughterhouse thanks to its great size. It is almost 2 meters tall and weighs 1.4 tonnes. Its name is Knickers and it will live out its days in Perth, Australia. Difficult words: bullock (a bull that was castrated – when an animal cannot make babies because people took those body parts away), escape (avoid, stay away from), slaughterhouse (a place where animals are slaughtered – killed for food). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about a bullock . It is from Perth in Australia. It is very big. It is 2 meters tall. It weighs 1.4 tonnes. Its name is Knickers. It is too big for the slaughterhouse . It will continue to live. Difficult words: bullock (a bull that cannot make babies because people took some of its body parts away), slaughterhouse (a place where animals are killed for food), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Four hundred chefs in Buenos Aires teamed up to beat the world record for pizzas made in 12 hours. Using more than 3 tonnes of flour , 2.7 tonnes of cheese and 88,000 olives, the team managed to produce 11,287 pizzas. Fourteen industrial-sized ovens allowed them to bake six pizzas a minute, and they beat the previous record by more than 1,000 pizzas. Difficult words: chefs (a professional cook), flour (white material, which looks like sand, and is used for making pizza or bread or other foods). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Four hundred chefs in Buenos Aires, Argentina, teamed up to make pizzas together. They wanted to beat the world record for the most pizzas made in 12 hours. They used 3 tonnes of flour , 2.7 tonnes of cheese and 88,000 olives. They also used 14 industrial-sized ovens which baked six pizzas a minute. In the end, they beat the record by more than 1,000 pizzas – they made 11,287 pizzas! Difficult words: chefs (a professional cook), flour (white material, which looks like sand, and is used for making pizza or bread), industrial-sized (very big – used in factories which make many pizzas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Four hundred chefs in Buenos Aires, Argentina, come together. They want to set a new world record. It is the record for the most pizzas made in 12 hours. They use 3 tonnes of flour , 2.7 tonnes of cheese and 88,000 olives. They have 14 very big ovens . These ovens make six pizzas a minute. In the end, the chefs set a new world record. They make 11,287 pizzas. Difficult words: chefs (a professional cook), flour (a white material, which looks like sand, and is used for making pizza or bread), oven (a machine which gets hot to bake/make a pizza or other food). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Seven young people aged 13 to 24 in the UK hear the words ‘you have cancer’ every day. Teenage Cancer Trust is the only UK charity dedicated to providing vital care for them. It funds specialist nurses, youth support teams, and unique hospital units that feel more like home than hospitals. The charity faces immense challenges, with cancer cases among young people rising and funding harder to secure. CEO Kate Collins highlights the urgent need for support. The impact of their services is profound . Ben, diagnosed at 21, found hope through their Cardiff unit, saying, ‘It changed my outlook and helped me connect with others who understood.’ Chloe, now cancer-free, recalls how the Bristol ward and its community kept her going during treatment. Young people need the charity more than ever during the time of challenges. Every donation not only supports services but raises awareness of the challenges young people with cancer face, ensuring no young person battles alone. Difficult words: vital (necessary), immense (extremely large or great), profound (very great or intense), ward (a separate room in a hospital). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Every day in the UK, seven people aged 13 to 24 hear that they have cancer. Teenage Cancer Trust is the only charity in the UK which helps them with nurses, youth workers, and special hospital spaces. These services aim to help young people continue their lives despite cancer. The charity’s leader says that more young people have cancer, and at the same time, there is a problem with money. It is a tough time for the organization, but young people need it more than ever. The charity runs 28 hospital units across the UK. These units help young people feel comfortable, meet others of their age, and get good care. Donations to the charity will help keep these services and make people understand what teen cancer patients go through. Difficult words: charity (an organization which helps people in need), youth (the time between being a child and adult), donation (money or things which you give to help a person or organization). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Teenage Cancer Trust is helping young people with cancer. Every day, seven young people in the UK, aged 13 to 24, hear they have cancer. Teenage Cancer Trust is the only charity in the UK which helps them. The charity provides nurses, youth workers, and special hospital spaces. These places feel more like home. Young people feel less alone. They get a good care. Ben Peters, who gets cancer at 21, says that the charity helps him feel better and make friends. More young people have cancer nowadays . The government does not have enough money. You can help the charity yourself and help young people. Difficult words: charity (an organization which helps people in need), provide (to give something to someone who needs it), nowadays (at present). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Panama recently marked the 25th anniversary of gaining control of the Panama Canal. The United States handed it over on December 31, 1999, but President-elect Donald Trump has threatened to reclaim it. During the anniversary ceremony, Panama’s President declared the canal would always remain under Panama’s control. The canal has a long history, starting with a failed French construction effort in the 19th century due to diseases that killed thousands of workers. The US completed it by 1914, connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and transforming global trade. Although Trump claims the US gets unfair fees and alleges Chinese influence over the canal, there is no evidence supporting these accusations. Under current treaties , the US can only intervene if neutrality is threatened but cannot reclaim control. The canal remains crucial to global trade. Over 70% of its traffic is linked to the US, which highlights its ongoing geopolitical importance. Difficult words: allege (to claim without proof), treaty (a formal agreement between countries), crucial (very important). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Panama celebrated 25 years of controlling the Panama Canal, which the US gave back on December 31, 1999. Donald Trump says the US should take the canal back. At the ceremony, Panama’s President promised the canal would always belong to Panama. The canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and is very important for world trade . The US built it in 1914 after a French project failed because many workers died from diseases. Trump says Panama charges high fees for US ships and that China has influence. But there is no proof of that. Currently, the US can act only if the canal’s fairness is at risk. The canal is still a key part of global trade and politics, 70% of all ships which go through do business with the US. Difficult words: trade (business activities), fail (to not be successful), proof (a fact or piece of information which shows that something is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Panama is celebrating 25 years of owning the Panama Canal . On December 31, 1999, the US give it back to Panama. President Trump now says the US should take it back. But Panama says it will keep the canal forever. The canal joins the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. It helps ships move faster. The US builds it in 1914. France fails to build the canal earlier. Many workers get sick and die. Trump says Panama wants too much money for US ships and that China has control. But there is no information about this. Panama says the canal is theirs. Rules only let the US act if the canal is in trouble. The canal is very important for trade all over the world but 70% of all the ships do business with the US. Difficult words: canal (a thin stretch of water for ships to travel along), act (to do something), trade (business activity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Liam Payne, the famous One Direction singer, died on October 6 after falling from a third-floor hotel balcony in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Following a thorough investigation, five people have been charged in connection with his death. Among the accused are Gilda Martin, the hotel manager, Esteban Grassi, the receptionist, and Roger Nores, Payne’s friend. They have been charged with manslaughter for failing to care for Liam, who was reportedly intoxicated . Two other individuals, Ezequiel Pereyra, a hotel worker, and Braian Paiz, a waiter, face charges for supplying drugs to Payne. The investigation revealed that Payne had taken a taxi to buy drugs before the incident. Authorities believe he may have fallen while trying to leave his hotel room. There is a strong interest in the case because of Payne’s popularity, and it is being handled by a national court. Difficult words: manslaughter (killing someone without planning it), intoxicated (drunk or affected by alcohol or drugs). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Liam Payne, the One Direction singer, died on October 6 after falling from a third-floor balcony in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Five people are in trouble because of his death. The hotel manager, Gilda Martin, receptionist Esteban Grassi, and Payne’s friend, Roger Nores, are charged with manslaughter . It means they didn’t take care of Liam when he was drunk . Two other people, Ezequiel Pereyra, who worked at the hotel, and Braian Paiz, a waiter, are charged with giving drugs to Liam. They found out that Liam bought drugs before the fall. The police think he fell while trying to leave his room. A big court is handling this case because many people loved Liam Payne. Difficult words: manslaughter (killing someone without planning it), drunk (losing control of yourself because you drank alcohol), charged (when authorities formally accuse someone of doing something wrong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Liam Payne, a singer from One Direction, dies on October 6. He falls from a hotel balcony in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Five people are in trouble because of his death . The hotel manager, Gilda Martin, a receptionist, Esteban Grassi, and Liam’s friend, Roger Nores. These people do not help Liam when he is drunk . Two others, Ezequiel Pereyra and Braian Paiz, give drugs to Liam. The police think that Liam buys drugs just before he dies. They believe that Liam falls because he is trying to leave his room. Many people love Liam. A big court is studying his death. Difficult words: death (when someone dies), drunk (when you drink too much alcohol), study (to look at carefully). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The German government has accused Elon Musk of attempting to influence the upcoming federal election by endorsing the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party on X. Musk claimed that only the AfD can save Germany, sparking criticism from Berlin. Germany’s Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution is monitoring the AfD for suspected ties to extremism . This controversy arises ahead of early elections on February 23, following the collapse of Chancellor Olaf Scholz’s coalition government over economic disputes. Scholz addressed the nation in his New Year’s speech, urging voters to stand united and reject manipulation from social media platforms or their owners. While he didn’t name Musk directly, he emphasized the importance of free and fair elections. The German government continues to use platforms like X to communicate its policies despite concerns about misinformation. Officials argue that leaving these platforms would limit their ability to reach people. Difficult words: endorse (to support someone publicly), extremism (very extreme political or religious beliefs), controversy (public disagreement or argument about something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The German government says Elon Musk is trying to influence their election because he supports the far-right AfD party on X. Musk wrote that only the AfD could save Germany, which worried officials. Authorities watch the AfD because of possible links to extremism . Germany will vote on February 23 after Chancellor Olaf Scholz’s government collapsed. In his New Year’s speech, Scholz asked people to stay united and not let social media platforms or their owners control the elections. He didn’t speak about Musk directly but about the importance of fair elections. The government is worried about false information on X, but they still use it to share news because it helps them speak to the public . Difficult words: extremism (very strong ideas and opinions about politics or religion), importance (how important something is), public (all people in general). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Germany says that Elon Musk is trying to change their elections . Elon Musk is the boss of social media platform X. Musk likes the far-right AfD party on X. He says that only the AfD can save Germany. Authorities are watching the AfD. They worry that the party has extreme ideas. Germany will vote on February 23. The government breaks up last month. Chancellor Olaf Scholz talks to people. He tells people to vote and not believe what social media says. Germany needs fair elections. The government is worried about false information on X. But they still use it to talk to people. Difficult words: elections (when people vote to choose leaders), far-right (having strong opinions about politics or religion), extreme (strong or very unusual). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

New Year’s Eve celebrations in Southern California brought concerns about air pollution and wildfire risks due to the widespread use of fireworks. Air quality in Los Angeles was expected to reach unhealthy levels during the celebrations. According to the South Coast Air Quality Management District (AQMD), fireworks release large amounts of fine particle pollution and metal air pollutants , which can harm health. Additionally, fireworks increase the risk of wildfires. The National Weather Service had issued a red flag warning for areas like the San Gabriel and Santa Monica mountains due to strong winds, dry conditions, and low humidity . These conditions make it easier for fires to start and spread. Authorities advised against using fireworks or other fire-starting materials, warning that individuals caught with illegal fireworks might face fines or jail time. A no-burn order was in place to reduce pollution and fire risks. Difficult words: pollutant (a substance that makes air or water dirty), humidity (the amount of water in the air). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

New Year’s Eve in Southern California brought worries about air pollution and wildfires. Experts expected that air quality in Los Angeles could become unhealthy during the celebrations. Fireworks cause a lot of pollution, including small particles and metals which can harm health. Fireworks can also start wildfires. The National Weather Service has warned about dangerous fire conditions in areas like the San Gabriel and Santa Monica mountains. Dry weather, strong winds, and low humidity make it easier for fires to start and spread. Authorities told people not to use fireworks or anything that could cause a fire. Anyone caught with illegal fireworks could get a fine or go to jail. Difficult words: pollution (dirty air, water, or land), particle (a small object), humidity (water in the air). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Southern California, fireworks for New Year’s Eve caused problems. The air in Los Angeles is not safe to breathe. Fireworks make the air dirty. They put small objects and metals in the air. It is bad for health and for the natural world too. Fireworks can also start fires. Some areas, like the San Gabriel Mountains, are very dry and windy. Fires can spread quickly. Authorities ask people not to use fireworks or anything that can make a fire. If someone has illegal fireworks, they could get a fine or go to jail. Difficult words: spread (to move to a larger area), illegal (not allowed), fine (money you must pay if you break a rule). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The world welcomed 2025 with diverse celebrations. In New York, crowds gathered at Times Square for the traditional ball drop, while fireworks lit up cities like Pittsburgh and Boston. Auckland, the first major city to celebrate, showcased fireworks from Sky Tower and recognized Indigenous tribes through light displays. Celebrations in Australia included fireworks in Sydney Harbor, performances, and Indigenous ceremonies. Meanwhile, Asia saw Japan preparing for the Year of the Snake, Bangkok hosting concerts, and Jakarta featuring drone shows. Amid festivities , conflict dampened celebrations in Ukraine, Gaza, and Lebanon. In Europe, Paris had a grand fireworks show on the Champs-Élysées, while London hosted a pyrotechnic display along the Thames. Rio de Janeiro celebrated with concerts and fireworks on Copacabana Beach, and Spain followed its tradition of eating 12 grapes for luck. Despite challenges worldwide, millions embraced the new year with hope. Difficult words: festivity (celebrating a special occasion), dampen (to make something less lively or strong), pyrotechnic (relating to fireworks). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The new year started with big events around the world. New York City had a ball drop at Times Square, and cities like Boston and Pittsburgh had fireworks. Auckland was the first big city to celebrate, with fireworks at Sky Tower and shows for Indigenous tribes . In Sydney, people enjoyed fireworks and music. Bangkok and Jakarta also had live performances and light shows. In Europe, Paris had fireworks, and London had a show on the Thames. Some places, like Ukraine and Gaza, had quieter celebrations because of war. In Rio de Janeiro, there were concerts and fireworks on the beach. In Spain, people ate 12 grapes at midnight for good luck. Even with problems, many celebrated with happiness. Difficult words: Indigenous (living in a land from the earliest times), tribe (a group of people who have the same history and culture), performance (a show for an audience). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People all over the world celebrate the new year. In New York, people watch the ball drop. Boston and other cities have fireworks . Auckland is the first city to have fireworks at Sky Tower. In Sydney, people watch fireworks and music shows. Paris has fireworks, and London has a big light show on the Thames. In Rio, people party on the beach and watch concerts. Some places, like Gaza, are not happy because of war. In Spain, people eat 12 grapes at midnight for good luck . Even with problems, people are happy to start the new year. Difficult words: firework (colorful lights in the sky), party (to have a good time at a party or other event, usually with drinking and music), good luck (when good things happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Norovirus, also called the winter vomiting disease, is a very infectious virus. It causes symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and stomach pain. The CDC reports that recent cases have risen sharply in the US, with 91 cases recorded in early December, nearly three times the weekly average between 2021 and 2024. Although it usually clears up quickly, it can be dangerous for infants or the elderly due to dehydration . To avoid catching norovirus, wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water, as alcohol-based sanitizers are ineffective. Be careful when preparing food and sanitize surfaces. You might remain contagious for a few days after symptoms stop. Other respiratory viruses, such as flu, COVID-19, and RSV, are also spreading. Vaccinations are available for all three, with specific recommendations for children, pregnant people, and older adults. Masks and testing help reduce risk, especially for vulnerable groups . Difficult words: dehydration (loss of too much water from the body), sanitizer (special liquid or gel that cleans hands), contagious (able to spread from one person to another), vulnerable group (people who are easily harmed or affected). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Norovirus is spreading quickly in the US. There were 91 cases in one week in December, much more than usual. The virus makes people feel sick with vomiting, diarrhea , and stomach pain. Most people get better quickly, but small children and older people can get very sick if they lose too much water. To stop the virus, wash your hands with soap and water because sanitizers don’t work well. Clean places where you prepare food, and be careful when you are still sick because you can pass it on even a few days after symptoms stop. Flu, COVID-19, and RSV are also spreading. Vaccines are the best way to stay safe. Masks and testing are also helpful, especially for people who could get very sick. Difficult words: diarrhea (watery stool), sanitizer (special liquid or gel which cleans hands), symptom (a physical or mental change which disease causes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Norovirus is making people sick in the US. There are more cases now than usual. There are 91 cases in one week. The virus makes you sick, with diarrhea , and stomach pain. Most people get better fast. But babies and old people can get very sick if they lose a lot of water. To stop the virus, wash your hands with soap and water. Hand gels do not work well. Be careful when you make food. Keep everything clean. You can still make others sick some days after you feel better. Flu, COVID-19, and RSV are also a problem. Vaccines can help keep you safe. Masks and tests are good for people who could get very sick. Difficult words: case (one sick person), diarrhea (watery stool), vaccine (a shot to stop sickness). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People found a turtle with multiple fractures on its shell, making healing difficult, but by working with a Lego enthusiast , the turtle received a custom wheelchair. The Lego frame sits on wheels which help the turtle get off the ground, and epoxy resin , surgical wire, and plumber’s putty holds all of it in place. The Maryland Zoo helped the injured wild Eastern Box Turtle recover while retaining its usual walking pace . Difficult words: enthusiast (somebody who is enthusiastic about something – loves doing it very much), custom (specially made), epoxy resin (a type of glue), putty (a type of paste which you can give a shape before it gets hard), pace (speed). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Every year, millions of Christmas trees end up in landfills, but an Illinois farm has a greener solution: feeding them to Nigerian pygmy goats! Urban Growers Collective, a nonprofit in Chicago, is accepting undecorated pine trees at South Chicago Farm until January 11. These trees are a nutritious snack for their 15 goats, providing vitamins A and C while promoting digestive health and reducing parasites. Goats love eating the bark, branches, and needles, which act as natural composters . However, donated trees must be free of decorations, tinsel , hooks, or fire-retardant sprays , as these can harm the animals. For those unable to donate trees to the farm, Chicago’s citywide recycling program runs from January 11–25, offering 27 drop-off sites. Recycled trees will be turned into mulch for parks, forests, and residents. Even broken holiday lights can be recycled at over 30 locations across Chicago through January 31, ensuring a more sustainable holiday season. Difficult words: composter (natural material that decomposes into soil), tinsel (long, shiny, colored string used as a decoration at Christmas), fire-retardant spray (a chemical spray that reduces fire risk), mulch (ground-up wood or leaves used in gardening). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Poncho, an eight-year-old cocker spaniel, went viral thanks to his life-saving CPR skills. At a display of police dog skills in Madrid, the dog ran to his partner when he collapsed lifeless on the floor. The dog quickly began CPR, leaping and thudding onto the officer’s chest and even nestling his head onto the fallen policeman’s neck, as if he was checking for a pulse. Poncho repeated the procedure until his friend revived , and the crowd roared with applause. Difficult words: CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation – making the heart and breathing work again), leap (jump up high), thud (move, fall down), nestle (put something closely), revive (bring to life again), roar (be loud). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has set a record by flying closer to the Sun than any other spacecraft. On Christmas Eve, it reached just 6.1 million km from the Sun’s surface, enduring temperatures of 1,400°C and harmful radiation that could have damaged its systems. Traveling at 692,000 kph, it became the fastest human-made object, equivalent to flying from London to New York in under 30 seconds. The probe survived thanks to a heat shield that kept its instruments cool. Scientists believe the data it collects will help answer why the Sun’s outer atmosphere, the corona , is much hotter than its surface. The corona, reaching millions of degrees, is key to understanding solar flares, magnetic fields , and space weather that affect Earth. Initial data will be analyzed starting in January, providing insights into the Sun’s behavior and its impact on our planet. Difficult words: radiation (energy from the Sun that can harm electronics), corona (the outermost layer of the Sun’s atmosphere), magnetic field (an invisible force around magnetic objects). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: probe (spacecraft), radiation (dangerous energy from the Sun), shield (a piece of metal or other material which protects someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This year brought many exciting advancements. Technological innovations included a titanium heart that kept a man alive until a transplant, and AI tools that improved cancer detection by identifying early warning signs. In medicine, groundbreaking trials included the first lung cancer vaccine, designed to help the immune system fight cancer cells. Besides this, Manuka honey was found to reduce breast cancer cell growth by 84%. A breakthrough in cervical cancer treatment reduced mortality by 40% with a new chemo-radiation method. In environmental progress, deforestation in the Amazon decreased by 31%, while efforts to restore the Great Barrier Reef included planting heat-resistant coral. Solar power grew rapidly, and China built the world’s largest solar farm. Social advancements included Thailand passing a same-sex marriage bill and the US capping insulin prices. Finally, space exploration achieved milestones like the first civilian spacewalk and NASA’s Solar Sail System for sunlight-powered spacecraft. Difficult words: groundbreaking (innovative and new), mortality (death rate), cap (to place a limit or restriction on prices). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The environment improved with less deforestation in the Amazon and new ways to save coral reefs. Solar power grew fast, with China building the biggest solar farm ever. Space had exciting news too, with the first civilian spacewalk and a new solar-powered spaceship idea from NASA. Social changes included Thailand’s new law for same-sex marriage and cheaper insulin for people in the US. Difficult words: cervical (relating to the cervix, the narrow lower part of the uterus), deforestation (clearing a wide area of trees), civilian (an ordinary person, not a soldier), insulin (a hormone which manages your blood sugar level). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
